newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bourse to self-govern, go scripless.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bourse to self-govern, go scripless.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) is expected to become a self-regulatory organisation and start scripless trading by November, bourse president Eduardo de los Angeles said on Tuesday.

At present, the bourse is under the direct supervision of the watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which has led to several conflicts between the two agencies over terms of listing and disclosure requirements.
Under its self-regulatory status, the 15-member board of the PSE will have the final say on matters concerning stock brokering and disclosure of information by all listed companies.
"Hopefully on November 11, the 50th anniversary of the SEC, (the agency) would designate the PSE as a self-regulatory organisation," De los Angeles told a morning television show.
The compliance and surveillance mechanism has been overhauled, although it still needs further strengthening, de los Angeles said.

"In our experience, there's still hesitancy to actually disclose many things. There is certain material information that they (listed companies) still would like to withold. In general, people want to paint a rosy picture about their business," he said.
De los Angeles said the exchange wanted to have private sector representation on its board of directors.
"The exchange is thinking of having three non-brokers on the board out of 15 (members)," he said.
De los Angeles also said that scripless trading could start on November 11.
"I have suggested to (SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay) that the central depository house be switched on...on the same date. This will usher in the scripless environment in the Philippines," he said.

At present, a stock certificate can be issued 28 days after the transaction. The central depository would eliminate the issuance of stock certificates and just use the book-entry system for every transaction.
